learning_objective: 🎯 See what happens when scientific brilliance meets a lawless mind! Explore the adventures and chaos created by an invisible man.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Griffin is a brilliant scientist who discovers rare drugs that make the human body transparent like glass. However, he is a lawless and angry person.
His landlord dislikes him and tries to evict him. In revenge, Griffin sets the house on fire, swallows his drugs, removes his clothes, and becomes an invisible, homeless wanderer in London.
Since it is freezing winter, he breaks into a big London store for clothes and food. He later robs a theatrical company to get bandages for his face, fake nose, glasses, and a hat.
He moves to an inn in Iping village. When his money runs out, he invisibly robs a clergyman's desk. The innkeeper (Mrs. Hall) finds his room empty, and the furniture mysteriously 'attacks' her!
The village constable, Mr. Jaffers, arrives to arrest him. Griffin starts removing his clothes, becoming invisible piece by piece, knocks Jaffers unconscious, and escapes again.

fun_activity.title: 👻 If You Were Invisible...
fun_activity.instructions: Griffin used his invisibility to steal and hit people. If you became invisible for one day, write down 2 good, helpful things you would do for society!

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast Griffin's brilliance as a scientist with his failure as a human being (lawless, selfish).
📌 Describe the episode with Mrs. Hall's furniture—how the chair 'sprang into the air' and pushed her out.
📌 Understand why Griffin had to be completely naked to be fully invisible, making winter a terrible time for him.
quick_recap: ⭐ The story is an excerpt from H.G. Wells' famous novel 'The Invisible Man'.
⭐ Two boys in London are the first to spot the muddy 'footprints without feet'.
⭐ Science is a tool; whether it is good or bad depends on the person using it.
